rows.question: why are ppl in latam cancelling lately?
rows.answer:
Looking at recent LATAM cancellations, the pattern has shifted dramatically:

**Most recent (November 2026):** "Not using" and "content" are tied at the top with **9 cancellations each**, followed by "other" and "competitor" at 6 each.

**The big story:** In **June and July 2026**, **price** was the overwhelming reason—**252 cancellations** in June and **86** in July. This has since dropped sharply to just 1-11 per month in August-November.

**Current trend (last 3 months):** The reasons are now more balanced across:
- Content dissatisfaction (28-32/month)
- Not using the service (26-29/month)  
- Competition (14-30/month)
- Technical issues (11-14/month)

It looks like there may have been a price increase or currency issue in mid-2026 that caused a spike, but lately cancellations have normalized with content selection and lack of engagement being the main drivers.

rows.question: is Larkspur Motors getting what they paid for? delivered vs ordered impressions
rows.answer:
No, Larkspur Motors is **not** getting what they paid for. They ordered **45,266 impressions** worth **$979.03**, but only received **31,682 impressions** worth **$685.13** — a **70% delivery rate** with a shortfall of **13,584 impressions** and **$293.90** in value.

## Key findings:

**Consistent underdelivery:** Every single one of their 30 campaigns delivered between **69.4% and 70.1%** of ordered impressions. This pattern held across:
- All campaign types (Awareness, Consideration, Conversion, Brand Launch)
- All time periods (2024 through 2026)
- All campaigns marked as "Completed" with no cancellations

**The 30% gap is systematic**, not isolated to specific campaigns or periods. This suggests an account-wide delivery constraint rather than individual campaign issues.

## What the data shows:

| Metric | Amount |
|--------|--------|
| Ordered impressions | 45,266 |
| Delivered impressions | 31,682 |
| Delivery rate | **70.0%** |
| Undelivered impressions | 13,584 |
| Contracted value | $979.03 |
| Delivered value | $685.13 |
| Value gap | **$293.90** |

**Note:** The data shows contracted values but not actual invoices or payments, so whether Larkspur was billed for the full amount or only for delivered impressions cannot be confirmed from these tables.

## Key findings:

**Consistent underdelivery:** Every single one of their 30 campaigns delivered between **69.4% and 70.1%** of ordered impressions. This pattern held across:
- All campaign types (Awareness, Consideration, Conversion, Brand Launch)
- All time periods (2024 through 2026)
- All campaigns marked as "Completed" with no cancellations

**The 30% gap is systematic**, not isolated to specific campaigns or periods. This suggests an account-wide delivery constraint rather than individual campaign issues.

| Metric | Amount |
|--------|--------|
| Ordered impressions | 45,266 |
| Delivered impressions | 31,682 |
| Delivery rate | **70.0%** |
| Undelivered impressions | 13,584 |
| Contracted value | $979.03 |
| Delivered value | $685.13 |
| Value gap | **$293.90** |

**Note:** The data shows contracted values but not actual invoices or payments, so whether Larkspur was billed for the full amount or only for delivered impressions cannot be confirmed from these tables.

  FROM `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`hoshi_distribution`.`playback_session` ps
  JOIN `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`hoshi_content`.`content_episode` ce ON ps.`content_episode_id` = ce.`content_episode_id`

  WHERE ps.`session_start_timestamp` >= '2026-10-01' AND ps.`session_start_timestamp` < '2026-11-01'
)
SELECT
  ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN has_avod THEN s END)/3600.0, 1) AS avod_title_watch_hours,

  ROUND(SUM(s)/3600.0, 1) AS total_watch_hours,
  ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN has_avod THEN s END)/SUM(s), 1) AS pct_of_total
FROM oct

## October 2026 watch hours from titles with an active AVOD window

Titles that currently have at least one active AVOD window brought in **2,468.7 watch hours** in October 2026. That is **18.4%** of the 13,404.7 total watch hours for the month, and it came from 220 such titles. **How I counted it**
- **Active AVOD window:** the window type is `AVOD` and the active flag is true, which means the window is open now. Every window with this flag also has the status "Active". 260 titles meet this today. [Query Result](https://example-workspace.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/78763f45a77a4239a4616ea7c174ff9c?o=0000000000000000#embed-query_6c1dc4)
- **Matching rule:** a title counts if it has an active AVOD window in any territory or on any platform. I did not require the viewing session to happen in the same territory or on the same platform as the window. If a title has several active AVOD windows, its watch time is still counted only once.
- **Watch hours:** the seconds actually watched in each session, divided by 3,600. A session falls in October when it started between 1 and 31 October 2026.
- **About the role of the viewing data:** the approved tables have no watch-time data. The hours come from the viewing-session table, which the scope rules allow only for joining. Here the approved content window table decides which titles count, and the viewing-session and episode tables add the watch hours.
